A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HUB/ATS research. All 14 pages of v2 and 20 pages of v3, including figures, equations, proofs, and supplementary experiments, support comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original simulations of paper recommendation, vaccine testing, and teacher-noise estimation, plus teacher-selection, rollout-policy, and query-cost analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices 9–10, including the teacher-noise estimation simulations.

M1.justification: The HUB-to-POMDP conversion, POMCPOW solver with best-arm rollouts, naive inference algorithm, and teacher-rationality estimator are retained. Expanded explanations do not establish an algorithmic revision.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same simulated paper-recommendation tasks, COVID-19 vaccine-testing task, and teacher-noise estimation scenarios. Moving experiments into the main text adds no task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Naive[50], Naive[100], Naive[200], Random, Random Arms, specific/general ATS, and the same rollout alternatives. Newly discussed related methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The 1000-step experiments, 20 recommendation problems, teacher rationalities, naive exploration horizons, vaccine parameters, and cost scaling are unchanged. v3's additional query-profile explanation does not establish a changed experimental procedure.

E4.justification: Specific versus general teacher selection, reward-estimation errors, action frequencies, rollout-policy comparisons, and query-cost sensitivity are all retained. v2 Appendix B becomes v3 Section 5.3; the rollout and cost appendices are renumbered.

E5.justification: Both versions retain 25-run averaging, 100 teacher-noise simulations, and Figure 4's median, IQR, whisker, and outlier conventions. No new empirical uncertainty or significance reporting appears.

E6.justification: Corresponding experimental plots contain identical graphics and retain the same findings, including ATS's recommendation advantage and Random Arms' slightly higher vaccine-trial return. The teacher-noise estimation mean squared error remains 0.061.

T1.justification: The existing definitions, four theorems, and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged. v3 adds conditions claimed to ensure worst-case accuracy p > 0.5 in Section 4.2 and an assertion of asymptotic Bayes-optimal action selection in Section 5.1, without a new proof.

C1.justification: The introduction strengthens v2's description of HUB as similar to a multi-armed bandit into an explicit claim that it strictly generalizes standard bandits. The central HUB/ATS contributions and teacher-selection benefit claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands applicability and limitations discussion: neural reward-model extensions, approximate posterior inference, finite-time optimality limitations, and demographic bias from rationality estimates and query costs. Section 7 adds concrete exclusion mechanisms and mitigation suggestions beyond v2's brief scalability paragraph.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly describes random query-pair selection and Bayesian updates over discretized spaces, while dropping v2's identification of the implementation as a Julia library. The code location and numerical experimental settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 Section 3 replaces the earlier IRL/crowdsourcing emphasis with extensive positioning against research on teacher and value heterogeneity, including Siththaranjan, Pitis, Poddar, and Shirali. It also newly explains how ATS relates to Barnett's myopic teacher-selection strategy.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and explanatory examples; expands preliminaries; and reorganizes theory, ATS evaluation, and vaccine testing. Related work and several appendix passages move into the main narrative, and the title and author details change.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes a single-column layout with widespread figure resizing and relocation. Figure 1 is redrawn and relabelled, and the specific/general comparison and vaccine results move from appendices into the main text. Experimental graphics are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves organization, research positioning, and scalability/bias discussion, but introduces a flawed theoretical qualification in Section 4.2. One nonrandom teacher and one unequal-utility pair do not ensure that the minimum accuracy over all teachers and pairs exceeds 0.5; the retained beta = 0 teacher already prevents this. With unchanged experimental evidence and proofs, these explanatory benefits and the new theoretical problem leave the net quality effect uncertain.
